chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Malik, who said: Ahmad ibn Maytham narrated to me, from Ubayd Allah ibn Musa, from Abd al-A'la ibn Hasin al-Tha'labi, from his father, who said:

I met Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali during a pilgrimage or a minor pilgrimage, and I said to him: 'My age has grown old and my bone has weakened, so I do not know if meeting you is decreed for me or not. Please make a covenant with me and inform me when the deliverance will be?'

He said: 'The homeless, the fugitive, the unique, the solitary, the one separated from his family, the one bereaved of his father, the one surnamed with his uncle's name, he is the master of the banners, and his name is the name of a prophet.'
I said: 'Repeat it to me.' So he called for a piece of leather or a tablet, and he wrote for me in it.

key_terms.الْأَدِيمُ: A piece of leather used as a writing surface
key_terms.الْفَرَجُ: Deliverance or relief, referring to the reappearance of the Imam
key_terms.الْمَمْتُورَ بِوَالِدِهِ: The one bereaved of his father (orphaned)
key_terms.الْمُكَنَّى بِعَمِّهِ: The one surnamed with his uncle's name
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الرَّايَاتِ: Master of the banners, a title for the leader who raises the standard of justice

ai.seo_question: What are the distinctive characteristics of the expected Imam regarding his name, family status, and title as described in this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Baqir identifies the Mahdi as a solitary, bereaved figure bearing the name of a prophet and the kunya of his uncle, emphasizing his unique status as the 'master of banners.' This description aligns with Shia eschatological traditions that link the Mahdi's identity to specific prophetic names and titles, reinforcing the concept of the Hidden Imam's eventual reappearance. The act of writing the description underscores the importance of preserving these signs during the period of concealment.
